title: test-0075-SOC-ECO-FOODSECURITY
passage: Many people mistakenly believe that food security simply means a village must grow all the food it eats to be safe. However, food security is actually about the availability, accessibility, and affordability of food for all people at all times. Even if a country has enough grain in its markets, individuals remain food insecure if they lack the money to purchase it. To prevent shortages, the government maintains a buffer stock of food grains, which is not for profit, but to ensure stable supplies during emergencies. Furthermore, the government operates a Public Distribution System through ration shops. These shops do not provide free food to everyone; instead, they offer essential items at subsidized prices specifically to families identified as living below the poverty line. By managing these stocks and targeting those in need, the government ensures that food reaches vulnerable populations, even when local production is low or market prices fluctuate. True food security is achieved when every person has the physical and economic means to obtain nutritious food, regardless of whether it was grown in their own village or transported from another region.
summary: Many people think that food security means that every village must grow all the food it needs to be safe. By managing these stocks and targeting those in need, the government ensures that food reaches vulnerable populations, even when local production is low or market prices fluctuate.
